source_text: ὁ ⸂τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν⸃ διὰ ⸂πνεύματος ἁγίου⸃ στόματος Δαυὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών· Ἱνατί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά;
english_snapshot: who[a], through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of David your servant, said: ‘Why did the nations rage[b], and the peoples devise vain things?’

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “our father David your servant,” making the introduction: “who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David your servant, said.”

source_text: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης ⸀χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
english_snapshot: Stephen[a], full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'full of faith and power' instead of 'full of grace and power.'

source_text: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν ⸀γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.
english_snapshot: This man led them out[a], performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and at the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.

signals.text: Or 'Reed Sea.' The Greek text reads 'Red Sea' (Ἐρυθρὰ Θάλασσα), the standard New Testament and Septuagint designation for the place of Israel's crossing.

source_text: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς ⸀τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν χριστόν.
english_snapshot: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Messiah to them[a][b].

signals.text: Or 'a city of Samaria.' The Greek can be understood as referring either to a particular city in Samaria or more generally to one of the cities of the Samaritan region.

source_text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ὑπέστρεφον εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα, πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν ⸀εὐηγγελίζοντο.
english_snapshot: So[a], after they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they were returning to Jerusalem[b], and were proclaiming the good news in many Samaritan villages.

signals.text: Or 'in many Samaritan villages.'

source_text: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος, Εἰ πιστεύεις ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας, ἔξεστιν. Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν, Πιστεύω τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἶναι τὸν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.
english_snapshot: And Philip[a] said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may.” And he answered and said, “I believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God.”

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 3rd-century papyri and the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations. It is present in the Byzantine majority tradition and the Latin tradition, and was cited by early church fathers like Irenaeus and Cyprian in the late 2nd century. It is often described by scholars as an early baptismal liturgical formula that was later incorporated into the narrative text of Acts.

source_text: ⸂Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο⸃.
english_snapshot: So then the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace and was being built up[a]; and walking in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit[b], it was multiplying.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the churches' instead of 'the church.'

source_text: ⸂τῇ δὲ⸃ ἐπαύριον ⸀εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν. ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους.
english_snapshot: On the next day he entered Caesarea[a]. Now Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.

signals.text: Greek has the singular verb 'he entered' but later the plural pronoun 'them,' likely focusing on Peter as the principal figure while including his companions in Cornelius's expectation.

source_text: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι, οἵτινες ⸀ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν ⸀καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ⸀Ἑλληνιστάς, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
english_snapshot: But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene[a], who, when they came to Antioch, were also speaking to the Hellenists, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Greeks' instead of 'Hellenists.' If that reading is original, the sense is that they were speaking to Gentiles, not only to Greek-speaking Jews.

source_text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν, ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, ⸀συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μᾶρκον.
english_snapshot: But Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem after completing the ministry, taking along John, who was called Mark.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'from Jerusalem' instead of 'to Jerusalem.'

source_text: καί, ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ,
english_snapshot: And for about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'he cared for them' instead of 'he put up with them.'

source_text: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου ⸀Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον, ἔλεγεν· ⸂Τί ἐμὲ⸃ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι; οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ· ἀλλ’ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετ’ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι.
english_snapshot: And as John was completing his course[a], he kept saying, ‘What do you suppose me to be? I am not he. But look, one is coming after me[b], the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

signals.text: Some manuscripts and translations render this more specifically as “to untie the strap of his sandals,” but the printed Greek text here reads simply “the sandal(s) of his feet ... to untie.”

source_text: ὅτι ταύτην ὁ θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις ⸀ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ⸂ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ⸃· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.
english_snapshot: that God has fulfilled this for our children by raising up Jesus[a], as it is also written in the second Psalm: ‘You are my Son[b]; today I have begotten you.’

signals.text: Or, 'to us, their children.' Some manuscripts read 'to our children,' while others support 'to us, their children.'

source_text: Ἐξιόντων δὲ ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ⸀ταῦτα.
english_snapshot: As they were going out[b][a], they were urging that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read more explicitly, 'As Paul and Barnabas were going out, the people were urging that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.'

source_text: ⸀καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον ⸀αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ⸀ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ⸀ὑμῶν.
english_snapshot: Yet he did not leave himself without witness[a], doing good by giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons[c][b], filling your hearts with food and gladness.

signals.text: Some translations render 'filling our hearts' instead of 'your hearts' because of a textual variant in the pronoun; the SBLGNT reads 'your hearts.'

source_text: γνωστὰ ἀπ’ ⸀αἰῶνος.
english_snapshot: known from of old[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read more fully, 'known from eternity' or 'who makes these things known from of old.'

source_text: Ἔδοξε δὲ τῷ Σίλᾳ ἐπιμεῖναι αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: But[a] it seemed good to Silas to remain there.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 3rd-century Papyrus 74, and the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations. It is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, some later Alexandrian and Western manuscripts, and the Latin and Syriac traditions. It was likely added by a later scribe to explain how Silas was still in Antioch to join Paul in verse 40, despite verse 33 stating that he and Judas had departed.

source_text: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ⸀ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ ⸂παντὸς προσώπου⸃ τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
english_snapshot: And he made from one man every nation of mankind to live on the whole face of the earth[a], having determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling place[b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'from one blood' instead of 'from one.' The main text follows the SBLGNT reading 'from one,' with 'man' supplied in English for clarity.

source_text: ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ ⸀πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος· καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ⸀ἔμελεν.
english_snapshot: Then they all seized Sosthenes[a], the synagogue ruler, and beat him in front of the tribunal. But Gallio paid no attention to these things.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'all the Greeks' instead of simply 'they all.' The earliest text is shorter and leaves the group's identity unspecified.

source_text: ⸂ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ⸃ ⸀εἰπών· ⸀Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου,
english_snapshot: but after taking leave and saying[a], “I will return to you again[b], if God wills,” he set sail from Ephesus.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'and saying, “I will return to you again, if God wills.”'

source_text: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί ⸀μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ ⸂καὶ θλίψεις με⸃ μένουσιν·
english_snapshot: except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in city after city[c][b][a], saying that chains and afflictions await me.

signals.text: Some manuscripts differ slightly in the placement/presence of 'me' with 'afflictions,' but the sense remains that chains and afflictions are awaiting Paul.

source_text: ⸀προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ ⸂αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου⸃.
english_snapshot: Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock[a], in which the Holy Spirit has appointed you overseers, to shepherd the church of God[c][b], which he obtained through the blood of his own.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the church of the Lord' instead of 'the church of God.'

source_text: ἐγένετο δὲ κραυγὴ μεγάλη, καὶ ἀναστάντες ⸂τινὲς τῶν γραμματέων⸃ τοῦ μέρους τῶν Φαρισαίων διεμάχοντο λέγοντες· Οὐδὲν κακὸν εὑρίσκομεν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ· εἰ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ἢ ⸀ἄγγελος—
english_snapshot: Then a great outcry arose[a], and some of the scribes of the party of the Pharisees stood up and contended, saying, “We find nothing wrong in this man[b]. But if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him—”

signals.text: Greek: 'But if a spirit spoke to him, or an angel—' The sentence breaks off abruptly in the Greek text.

source_text: ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ⸀ἐκρατήσαμεν,
english_snapshot: He even tried to defile the temple[a], and we seized him,

signals.text: Some manuscripts add a longer reading here, including that they wanted to judge Paul according to their law and that Lysias the commander took him from their hands.

source_text: παρελθὼν δὲ Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος μετὰ πολλῆς βίας ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν ἡμῶν ἀπήγαγεν,
english_snapshot: But[a] Lysias the commander came and took him out of our hands with great force,

signals.text: This verse (along with the end of verse 6 and the beginning of verse 8) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 3rd-century Papyrus 74 and the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations. It is preserved in the Byzantine majority tradition, the Latin tradition, and later Greek manuscripts. It reads as an early editorial expansion narrating the Roman commander's intervention before Felix.

source_text: παρ’ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: From him[a], by examining him yourself[b], you will be able to learn about all these things of which we accuse him.

signals.text: Some manuscripts include an additional clause in v. 7 about the commander Lysias taking Paul away by force and ordering the accusers to come before Felix; the SBLGNT text does not include that wording here.

source_text: μετ’ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατ’ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος ⸀Εὐρακύλων·
english_snapshot: But not long after[b][a], a typhonic wind called Euraquilo rushed down against it.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Euroclydon' instead of 'Euraquilo.'

source_text: Καὶ ταῦτα αὐτοῦ εἰπόντος, ἀπῆλθον οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, πολλὴν ἔχοντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς συζήτησιν.
english_snapshot: And when he had [a]said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

signals.text: This entire verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 3rd-century Papyrus 74, 4th-century Sinaiticus, and 4th-century Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations. It is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, as well as early Latin and Syriac translations. It is likely a later scribal expansion added to round out the narrative of the Jewish leaders' departure.
